newsitem.title: CUBA: British trade mission visits Cuba.
newsitem.headline: British trade mission visits Cuba.

text.p: A British trade mission led by Baroness Young, a senior member of Britain's ruling Conservative Party, began talks with Cuban officials on Monday aimed at increasing business between the two countries.

Young, who leads the Cuba Initiative, a government and private industry plan to increase trade ties with the communist-ruled island, was accompanied by about 10 representatives of firms from sectors such as hotel construction and finance.

Arriving in Havana late on Sunday for her third visit to Cuba, Young said she wanted to continue dialogue with Cuban officials and to increase trade between the two countries. She noted Britain was at odds with the United States over legislation to tighten a longstanding U.S. embargo.
The Helm-Burton law, which aims to discourage investment from third countries in Cuba, has been widely criticised by U.S. allies ranging from Canada and Mexico to members of the European Union.
The trade mission opened their talks with a meeting on Monday with Foreign Trade Minister Ricardo Cabrisas.
During her three-day visit, Young was also due to meet government officials including vice-president Carlos Lage, Foreign Minister Roberto Robaina and parliamentary president Ricardo Alarcon.
Bilateral trade was around $42 million last year and increased to $48 million in the period January-July this year, British officials said.
British firms have invested in areas such as oil exploration, tobacco and soap and detergent production. Figures on how much this investment is worth are not available.
